interactions.summary: The reading opens the terrace of gluttony with emaciated shades and Dante’s recognition of Forese by voice rather than face.
Jiang identifies Forese Donati as Dante’s childhood friend and situates him inside the Donati family network with Piccarda and Corso.
Forese explains that the tree and water renew the gluttons’ hunger as both pain and solace, since that longing guides them toward purification.

claims.claim: The gluttons are described as so emaciated that personhood survives more in voice and memory than in facial appearance.
Jiang identifies Forese as Dante’s childhood best friend and fellow poet, which raises the emotional temperature of the encounter beyond generic allegory.
Forese’s explanation treats the gluttony punishments as simultaneously painful and consoling because the same hunger that hurts them also guides them toward Christ and purification.

signature_moments.moment: Dante recognizes his friend only when the voice reignites the memory the face can no longer carry.
signature_moments.source_phrase: his voice made plain to me what his appearance had obliterated
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of the sharpest body-memory moments in the source, and it matters for the later soul/shade discussion.

signature_moments.moment: Punishment is renamed solace because longing itself is now aimed toward redemption.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I speak of pain, but I should speak of solace
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The line compresses Jiang’s recurring purgatory logic: suffering matters because it is voluntarily aligned with return.

chronology_notes.note: This packet begins the Forese encounter, which becomes Jiang’s June 26 bridge from abstract punishment to personal memory and prayer efficacy.
